chaines.hitbodedut_sihah: Say what is on your heart
chaines.hitbodedut_sihah_invite: Speak in your own language, as you would to someone. Everything on your heart, unrehearsed.
chaines.hitbodedut_harata_invite: Say what you regret, and say it plainly. Regret before Him is not a trial.
chaines.hitbodedut_bakasha_invite: Ask for what you lack, and first of all to be brought close to Him. Even what you believe yourself too far from.
chaines.hitbodedut_torah_invite: Take a teaching you heard today, and ask to reach it yourself.
chaines.hitbodedut_hodaa_invite: Give thanks for what you have been given, each as far as you are able. This is how you take leave.
chaines.onboarding_practice_body: Hitbodedut means withdrawing alone for a while each day and speaking to Hashem in your own language, as you would to someone. No formula to recite, no level to reach.
chaines.onboarding_private_body: The app asks for no Internet access at all. What you write stays on this phone, and only you can take it out, through the export.

chaines.tips_hint: Ten pointers, to begin and to keep going.
chaines.tip_1_body: The first step in hitbodedut is to find a quiet place where you can be alone with yourself and with Hashem. It does not have to be entirely isolated, but it must be somewhere you will not be interrupted. A free room at home, a quiet stretch of beach, a spot out in nature. If you can, choose a natural setting: nature itself can be a source of inner quiet.
chaines.tip_2_body: If you are new to this, start short. Give fifteen minutes a day to hitbodedut, and lengthen it little by little, up to an hour if you can. Do not jump straight to a long hitbodedut. Go step by step, so that it becomes a habit and not a burden. Fix a regular time, so the practice becomes part of your day rather than something random.
chaines.tip_3_body: Begin the hitbodedut by speaking to Hashem, in your own words, in a whisper if need be. Do not worry if at first you do not know quite what to say. Simply open your heart and begin. It can be asking forgiveness, a plain prayer about what you feel, or a thank you. Hitbodedut does not have to be orderly or planned in advance. It is a place to set down what is in your heart and to turn towards Hashem.
chaines.tip_4_body: If you want to feel truly alone with yourself, avoid devices entirely during hitbodedut. Turn the phone off, or leave it in another room. The freer you are of outside distraction, the better you will connect to yourself and to Hashem. Cutting off from the outside world helps you concentrate and settle into the quiet within.
chaines.tip_5_title: Start with Tehillim, or your own words
chaines.tip_5_body: If you are not sure how to begin, open Tehillim and read a few chapters. The Psalms are prayer already formed, very direct, and they touch the soul. In hitbodedut they can be a spiritual thread leading you straight to Hashem. And if you feel you have no words, you can simply speak with Hashem freely, sharing your thoughts and what you feel.
chaines.tip_6_body: During hitbodedut, ask yourself inward questions. What am I feeling right now? What am I going through? How can I feel closer to Hashem? What do I need to improve in my life? This is a time for a real heshbon nefesh. Sometimes, in the inner quiet, you come to see your real needs and the right direction for your life.
chaines.tip_7_body: During hitbodedut, do not try to hide from Hashem what you feel. This is a time when you are allowed to be honest with yourself and with Hashem. If you feel anger, frustration, fear or insecurity, this is the place to say it. Honesty is the key to spiritual growth. The more honest you are, the more inner quiet you will find.
chaines.tip_8_body: Hitbodedut can also be a time to make peace with yourself. That means being somewhere you are not judging, not criticizing, not angry at yourself. It is a time of reconciliation, where you forgive yourself, ask forgiveness for your mistakes, and resolve to mend your ways.
chaines.tip_9_body: Part of hitbodedut can be complete silence. When the words do not come, stay a while before Hashem without saying anything: being there, ready and wanting to speak, already counts (Likutei Moharan II, 25). In that silence, what is inside surfaces and comes clear.
chaines.tip_10_title: End with a deep breath and thanks
chaines.tip_10_body: At the end of hitbodedut, finish with a deep breath and bless Hashem for the time you spent together. It is a moment of thanks for the great gift of connection, and for the inner quiet you found. Even if you felt it was hard to find answers, do not worry: this meeting with yourself and with Hashem already brings spiritual abundance into your life.

chaines.onboarding_session_body: Pick a length, or an open hitbodedut, and a subject if you like. A niggun can play along. A word of chizuk opens and closes the hitbodedut, and if the words won’t come, a button is there to help.
chaines.onboarding_days_body: The streak counts your days in a row, and the week shows at a glance. After each hitbodedut, a note can go into your journal. Reminders nudge you at the time you choose.
chaines.onboarding_texts_body: Tikkun HaKlali, Tehillim, the siddur, Tefilot sorted by subject, a library and tips for hitbodedut, ready whenever you are.
chaines.onboarding_yours_body: In Settings: the language (French, English or Hebrew), the screen colors, your first name and your usual hitbodedut length. Music has its own section.
chaines.onboarding_adresse_body: At the end of each hitbodedut, the app congratulates you. Pick the word that fits you; you can change it in Settings.
chaines.onboarding_days_body_web: The streak counts your days in a row, and the week shows at a glance. After each hitbodedut, a note can go into your journal.
chaines.onboarding_private_body_web: What you write stays in this browser, on this device: nothing is sent anywhere.

chaines.rappel_pluie_debut_edot: %1$s, in the Arvit Amida, we begin to say the winter blessing “בָּרֵךְ עָלֵינוּ”.

chaines.rappel_pluie_fin_edot: From Pesach, we return to the summer blessing “בָּרְכֵנוּ”.
chaines.rappel_pluie_fin: From Pesach, we no longer ask for rain: “וְתֵן בְּרָכָה”.

chaines.rappel_guechem_fin: %1$s, at Musaf of the first day of Pesach, we stop saying “מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ וּמוֹרִיד הַגֶּשֶׁם”.
chaines.rappel_dix_jours: %1$s the Ten Days of Repentance begin: “הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ”, “הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט” and the additions to the Amida (“זָכְרֵנוּ”…).
